patches.find: add_library(cxx_static STATIC ${LIBCXX_SOURCES} ${LIBCXX_HEADERS})
patches.replace:
# CRT: cxx_static (unlike cxx_shared, just below -- deliberately left
# alone) does not need __crt_dso_handle.cpp's own __dso_handle definition
# on Linux: libc/src/arch/linux/common/cxa_atexit.c already provides one,
# with hidden visibility specifically so every *static* consumer that
# archives libc.a directly into its own final image gets its own private
# copy merged in at link time -- a real multiple-definition error the
# moment a static link pulled in both libc.a's copy and this one
# together (confirmed for real, 2026-08-25, finishing TODO.md's Linux
# item 6). cxx_shared cannot rely on that: it is a *separate* DSO image
# that never statically embeds libc.a's own object files (only links
# against libc.so at the DSO boundary), and a hidden-visibility symbol
# can never be resolved across a shared-object boundary by design -- so
# it still needs its own copy, unconditionally, exactly like macOS
# (whose crt1.o provides no __dso_handle at all, the original motivating
# reason this shim exists -- see that file's own comment and HISTORY.md's
# dated __dso_handle entries for the fuller story). Confirmed for real:
# omitting it from cxx_shared too produced "relocation R_X86_64_PC32
# against undefined hidden symbol `__dso_handle` can not be used when
# making a shared object" linking libc++abi.so (libcxxabi/recipe.json's
# own matching patch, same reasoning) -- a completely different failure
# mode from the static multiple-definition one, confirming the two
# targets genuinely need opposite treatment, not the same one.
set(CRT_LIBCXX_STATIC_SOURCES ${LIBCXX_SOURCES})
if (CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL "Linux")
  list(REMOVE_ITEM CRT_LIBCXX_STATIC_SOURCES __crt_dso_handle.cpp)
endif()
add_library(cxx_static STATIC ${CRT_LIBCXX_STATIC_SOURCES} ${LIBCXX_HEADERS})
patches.reason: Confirmed for real (2026-08-25) on Linux, finishing TODO.md's item 6 (the static imported-libc++ locale/iostream gap -- see ../libcxxabi/recipe.json's own matching patch for the fuller root-cause story, identical on both recipes): once the real missing-objects gap was fixed by a genuinely fresh rebuild, static linking a real program against sysroot/lib/libc++.a got past that and hit a NEW blocker next -- `multiple definition of __dso_handle` between libc.a's own copy (cxa_atexit.c) and this file's cxx_static copy. A first attempt guarded __crt_dso_handle.cpp's own *content* out entirely on Linux via #if !defined(__linux__) inside the file, but that broke cxx_shared instead (libc++.so's own build, a genuinely separate DSO that cannot reuse libc.a's hidden-visibility copy across the shared-object boundary) -- confirmed for real via the exact `undefined hidden symbol` linker error this reason field's own patch content quotes above. This CMake-level exclusion (only cxx_static's own source list, only on Linux) is the correct, narrower fix: cxx_shared keeps defining it unconditionally (matching macOS, which needs it on both target kinds since it has no libc.a __dso_handle to lean on at all), only cxx_static on Linux specifically omits it.

The cost is std::print's own native-Unicode WriteConsoleW() fast path on a real Windows console (__write_to_windows_console(), also gated by the same macro) -- accepted as a real, honest, narrow degradation (falls back to plain byte-oriented fwrite(), matching every other stream write this project already does) rather than either reimplementing MSVC's fd model or leaving the whole recipe unbuildable on Windows. A single #undef right after _LIBCPP_BEGIN_NAMESPACE_STD (rather than 6 separate find/replace patches at every individual _LIBCPP_WIN32API check in this file) is deliberately used to flip all of this file's own downstream dispatch consistently in one place, scope-checked to confirm nothing this header transitively includes reads the same macro. Confirmed for real (2026-08-31) on Windows: temp_directory_path() returned a single garbled character (e.g. just "C") instead of the real temp path -- traced to GetTempPathW (a real Win32 wide-string API, writing genuine 2-byte UTF-16) writing directly into a wchar_t[MAX_PATH] buffer, where this project's own wchar_t is 4 bytes (-fwchar-type=int). Each 4-byte "unit" then straddled two real UTF-16 code units, and the second half of the first real character (a zero high byte) was read back as an embedded NUL terminator. Fixed the same way as every other real Win32 wide-string API boundary in this recipe: a real char16_t scratch buffer is the actual GetTempPathW call target, widened into this project's own wchar_t buf afterward. See src/filesystem/crt_win32_wide.h's own extra_files entry (this recipe's own addition) for the shared narrow()/widen() helpers and their own fuller reasoning.

Unlike libc/hdr/'s own files, this one is not LIBC_FULL_BUILD-gated overlay-mode code -- it is real, always-needed content (plain macro/type definitions, confirmed as plain committed files, not .h.def templates needing generation). Fetched the whole directory rather than just llvm-libc-macros/ (which alone would have been enough for this one error) to front-load the very likely next miss, llvm-libc-types/ (a standard sibling in llvm-libc's own include/ layout) -- avoiding another full rebuild-and-discover round trip for a directory of comparable, still-bounded size (304 files total is not remotely close to needing the rest of llvm-libc's own OS-specific implementation).

libc/hdr added alongside libc/shared and libc/src/__support (2026-08-22, same session): libc/src/__support/CPP/limits.h's own #include "hdr/limits_macros.h" needs it, confirmed for real via `fatal error: 'hdr/limits_macros.h' file not found`. Small (66 files, confirmed via `git ls-tree -r`) and, unlike __support/, genuinely reassuring to depend on rather than just bounded: limits_macros.h's own content is a plain `#ifdef LIBC_FULL_BUILD ... #else #include <limits.h> #endif` -- llvm-libc's own "overlay mode" escape hatch, deliberately meant for exactly this project's own situation (reusing llvm-libc's portable support utilities layered on top of a real, independent host libc, never building the rest of llvm-libc itself). LIBC_FULL_BUILD is never defined anywhere in this project's own build, so every libc/hdr/*.h wrapper takes the "Overlay mode" branch -- confirmed on errno_macros.h too (same #ifdef LIBC_FULL_BUILD/#else/#include <errno.h>/#endif shape), and on one libc/hdr/func/*.h proxy (aligned_alloc.h), which instead of a direct #include <...> redirects to a sibling libc/hdr/*_overlay.h file within this same small directory -- still fully self-contained within the 66 files fetched here, not a further external dependency.

libc/src/__support added alongside libc/shared (2026-08-22, same session as the libc/shared fix just below): libc/shared/fp_bits.h's own #include "src/__support/FPUtil/FPBits.h" reaches further into llvm-libc's own internal support-utility tree, confirmed for real via `fatal error: 'src/__support/FPUtil/FPBits.h' file not found` the first time libc/shared alone was fetched. libc/src/__support/ (319 files total, confirmed via `git ls-tree -r`) is llvm-libc's own deliberately reusable, OS-independent low-level utility layer -- CPP/ (portable STL-shaped helpers: bit.h, type_traits.h, array.h, ...), macros/, math_extras.h, sign.h, uint128.h, etc. -- not the OS-specific syscall implementation the rest of llvm-libc's own src/ tree has, so fetching the whole subtree here (rather than chasing individual transitive headers one at a time) is a bounded, deliberate scope match to what FPBits.h actually needs, not a slippery-slope pull of all of llvm-libc. No new include path was needed for this addition: it resolves through the exact same CRT_LIBC_SHARED_PARENT_DIR (-I<...>/libc) the driver already adds for libc/shared, since "src/__support/..." is *also* rooted at that same libc/ parent directory.

build_targets no longer includes cxx_filesystem or cxx-generated-config (both present in the OLD recipe's own list, the second one Windows-only). Confirmed for real: `ninja -t targets` against this new source's own configured build tree lists only cxx, cxx_experimental, cxx_shared, cxx_static, cxx-test-depends -- neither name exists as a target at all any more, on any platform (surfaced as `ninja: error: unknown target 'cxx_filesystem'`, not a per-platform gate the way the OLD recipe's own Windows-only omission was). Matches a real, general modernization in current libcxx: C++17 <filesystem> is no longer a separate opt-in library needing its own build target.

generate-cxx-headers added to build_targets (2026-08-22, same session): correcting an overclaim in the note above -- header generation is NOT fully folded into cxx's own build graph. `cmake --install` failed after a full `cxx`+`cxx_experimental` build with `file INSTALL cannot find .../include/c++/v1/libcxx.imp: No such file or directory`. Confirmed via the real libcxx/include/CMakeLists.txt (fetched and read at this pinned commit): libcxx.imp is one output of add_custom_target(generate-cxx-headers ALL DEPENDS ${_all_includes}) -- an IWYU mapping file generated by utils/generate_iwyu_mapping.py, listed in install(FILES ... COMPONENT cxx-headers) alongside the real headers. The plain per-header copies DO get pulled in transitively by cxx/cxx_experimental (since compiling needs them), but this one extra generated file apparently isn't a hard dependency of the compiled objects themselves, so ninja never built it when only cxx/cxx_experimental were requested -- confirmed via the WSL build tree directly: the file was genuinely absent from the build dir (`ls .../include/c++/v1/ | grep imp` -> nothing) and no "Generate the mapping file for include-what-you-use" line ever appeared in the build log. `ninja -t targets all` confirms a plain `generate-cxx-headers: phony` alias exists (in addition to the subdir-prefixed `libcxx/include/generate-cxx-headers`), so requesting it directly as its own build target is the fix, not a deeper CMakeLists.txt change.

cmake.driver (new): the fetched libcxx/CMakeLists.txt at this commit no longer calls project() itself at all (confirmed by grepping the full ~860-line file for `^project(` -- zero matches) -- unlike the OLD platform/external/libcxx fork, which still carried its own standalone-build bootstrap (the exact asymmetry ../libunwind/standalone/CMakeLists.txt's own comment already described between libunwind and "the sibling libcxx/libcxxabi checkouts" was true when that comment was written, but libcxx has since converged onto the same monorepo-only, add_subdirectory()-only structure libunwind already had). LIBCXX_STANDARD_VER (removed): the previous pin (c++14) was chosen for a reason specific to the OLD, now-abandoned fork ("avoids the removed C11 gets() import") that does not obviously still apply to this genuinely different, actively-maintained source tree, and this CMake option controls the dialect libcxx's *own* .cpp implementation files are compiled with -- a materially different axis from _LIBCPP_STD_VER (which real *consumers* like Skia's own -std=c++20 TUs see, driven by their own compiler flag, not by how libcxx.a/.so itself was built). Left unset for now (upstream's own default) rather than carried forward on stale reasoning; revisit with a real, evidenced reason if the build actually needs an explicit value.

LIBCXX_CXX_ABI=system-libcxxabi (changed from the OLD recipe's own plain 'libcxxabi' value) -- a real, forced architectural finding, not a style choice. The new source's own libcxx/cmake/Modules/HandleLibCXXABI.cmake, included via libcxx/CMakeLists.txt's `include(HandleLibCXXABI)`, only wires up the plain 'libcxxabi' branch's libcxx-abi-shared/libcxx-abi-static targets `if (TARGET cxxabi_shared)`/`if (TARGET cxxabi_static)` -- i.e. it requires libcxxabi's own CMake targets to already exist in the *same* CMake project graph, which only a combined, single-configure "runtimes" build (libcxx+libcxxabi add_subdirectory()'d together under one project()) provides. This project's own architecture deliberately builds each recipe as a fully separate `cmake -S -B` invocation instead (see ../libunwind/recipe.json's own notes for why: no combined-runtimes-build machinery, by design), so that branch silently produced no libcxx-abi-shared/-static targets at all -- confirmed for real via `CMake Error ... Target "libcxx-abi-shared" not found` at libcxx/src/CMakeLists.txt's own add_custom_command generator-expression evaluation, plus a CMake Warning that LIBCXX_CXX_ABI_INCLUDE_PATHS/LIBCXX_CXX_ABI_LIBRARY_PATH (this recipe's own, still set) were going completely unused. The 'system-libcxxabi' branch is the one still designed for exactly this project's own case: a real, separately-built libc++abi provided out of tree, located by name+path rather than an in-process CMake target -- import_shared_library(libcxx-abi-shared c++abi)/import_static_library(..., c++abi) match this recipe's own libcxxabi output naming exactly (libc++abi.a/.so/.dll), and import_private_headers() copies exactly cxxabi.h/__cxxabi_config.h from LIBCXX_CXX_ABI_INCLUDE_PATHS -- both confirmed present in ../libcxxabi's own fetched include/ directory before making this change. LIBCXX_CXX_ABI_INCLUDE_PATHS/LIBCXX_CXX_ABI_LIBRARY_PATH themselves needed no change at all, only the LIBCXX_CXX_ABI value selecting which branch of HandleLibCXXABI.cmake consumes them.
